be5cdca3.title: Share rate, and does it vary by `status_share…

messages.content: Share rate, and does it vary by `status_shared` (do approvals get shared more)?

This can't be answered yet — the instrumentation it needs isn't live. I confirmed directly against the `clickathon` database (`list_tables` on all 17 tables, then a full column scan across every table) that no table or column contains "share" or "status" anywhere in its name or schema: the live tables are `destination_card_clicked`, `application_started`, `document_uploaded`, `pay_now_clicked`, `purchase_completed`, `search_typed`, `landing_page_scrolled`, `auth_completed`, the 5 Express Checkout tables, and the 4 Group/Family tables (`group_started`, `traveller_added`, `traveller_removed`, `group_submitted`) — none of them has a `status_shared` column, a `share_*` event, or anything resembling an approval-status field. The wiki's tables index and known_issues.md (checked in full) confirm the same 17-table inventory and don't reference a "share"/"approval" concept either — this appears to belong to a spec (e.g. a group/family approval-sharing feature) that hasn't been instrumented and loaded into this database yet.

To answer "share rate" and "does approval status affect share rate" once live, we'd need at minimum: an event marking an application/itinerary as shared (with a timestamp and an actor/recipient), plus the `status_shared` field (or equivalent approval-status column) on the shared entity, joinable via a stable key (per D2 in known_issues.md, watch for 32-char vs 36-char UUID `application_id` mismatches — that trap has broken every spec's join so far). Until that lands, no live number can be reported without fabricating one, so none is given here.
Reconversion (recovery) rate by **drop_step** — which step is most recoverable?

`application_started` is the most recoverable drop step at **4.80%** (25/521), essentially tied with `pay_now_clicked` at **4.79%** (19/397). `document_uploaded` trails a bit at **4.45%** (31/696), and `destination_card_clicked` is clearly the worst-recovering step at **2.62%** (18/686) — roughly half the rate of the other three. Overall recovery rate across all steps is 93/2,300 = 4.04%, matching the wiki's headline figure.

| drop_step | abandoned (n) | reconverted (n) | recovery rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| application_started | 521 | 25 | **4.80%** |
| pay_now_clicked | 397 | 19 | 4.79% |
| document_uploaded | 696 | 31 | 4.45% |
| destination_card_clicked | 686 | 18 | 2.62% |

Query: joined `clickathon.abandonment_detected` (2,300 rows, 1/user) to `clickathon.reconverted` (93 rows, 1/user) on `user_id`, grouped by `abandonment_detected.drop_step`. `user_id` was used deliberately instead of `application_id`, because `application_id` is confirmed 0% overlap against `application_started` for all 6 Abandoned Checkout Recovery tables (known_issues.md D2) — this spec must be analyzed standalone via its own `user_id`/`drop_step` keys.

This also **upgrades the wiki's caveat** on this figure: the tables/index and `abandonment_detected.md`/`reconverted.md` pages flag the recovery step-through as an "unverified row-count ratio" pending a set-membership check (D1) — that check has now run live. Result: **100% of `reconverted`'s 93 `user_id`s are a verified subset of `abandonment_detected`'s 2,300** (no orphans), and **100% of matched rows carry the same `drop_step`** in both tables (93/93) — so this breakdown is a genuine verified join, not a coincidental row-count ratio. Sample scope: Abandoned Checkout Recovery data, 2026-06-08 06:01 → 2026-07-01 00:00; n is small per step (397–696 abandoned, 18–31 recovered), so the gap between the top three steps (4.45–4.80%) should be read as noisy/near-tied, while `destination_card_clicked`'s clearly lower 2.62% is the more robust signal — users who drop at the very first step (before even starting an application) recover at roughly half the rate of those who dropped further into the funnel.

Built a 5-chart dashboard from live queries against `clickathon` (all verified by set-membership join per known_issues.md → D1, not `windowFunnel`, which loses 52% of true conversions on this data):

1. **Main visa funnel** (baseline, H1 2026): 1,000,000 card clicks → 154,413 applications (15.44%) → 20,446 doc uploads (13.24%) → 14,739 pay clicks (72.09%) → 7,054 purchases (47.86%). End-to-end `funnel_conversion` = 7,054/154,413 = **4.57%**.
2. **Group/Family completion rate by group size** (spec 02, 2026-06-08→06-28, 1,200 groups): monotonic decline from **69.47%** (size 2) to **31.11%** (size 6).
3. **Instant Forex attach rate by destination** (spec 05, same window, 2,900 offers shown): best **US 24.58%**, worst **AU 13.78%**, ~11pp spread across 14 destinations.
4. **Abandoned-checkout recovery rate by drop step** (spec 04, 2026-06-08→07-01, 2,300 abandonments): flat 4.45%–4.80% for the first three funnel steps, notably worse at **2.62%** for the earliest drop point (`destination_card_clicked`).
5. **Monthly funnel-conversion trend** (baseline, Jan–Jun 2026, July excluded as a 9-row partial fragment): a real portfolio-wide decline from **4.94%** (Jan) to **3.96%** (Jun), ~20% relative drop despite rising application volume — and per K4, not Schengen-specific (Schengen and other destinations track within ±0.3pp every month), so it remains genuinely unexplained.

Scope/caveats: charts 2–4 come from newly-instrumented spec tables whose `application_id` has **0% overlap** with the main funnel (known_issues.md → D2) — they are analyzed standalone via their own keys (`group_id`, `user_id`), not joined back to `destination_card_clicked`/`application_started`. All five charts' underlying counts were re-queried live on 2026-08-02 and match the wiki's previously-verified figures exactly.

See the full report: q02_report.html.

4e899b48.title: Analyze the existing funnel and surface the m…

messages.content: Analyze the existing funnel and surface the most important issues, with the why.

Scope: the core visa funnel — `destination_card_clicked → application_started → document_uploaded → pay_now_clicked → purchase_completed` — over the full H1 2026 baseline window (2025-12-31 23:41 → 2026-07-01, 1,000,000 users at the top). All numbers below were re-queried live just now by set membership (never `windowFunnel`/timestamp order — see D1: naive time-ordered funnel tools understate conversion by 52%, reporting 2.18% instead of the true 4.57%).

**Live-confirmed funnel:**

| Stage | Users | Step-through |
|---|---:|---:|
| destination_card_clicked | 1,000,000 | — |
| application_started | 154,413 | 15.44% |
| document_uploaded | 20,446 | **13.24%** |
| pay_now_clicked | 14,739 | 72.09% |
| purchase_completed | 7,054 | 47.86% |

Card→purchase: 0.71%. **Application→purchase (the default `funnel_conversion` metric): 4.57%.**

### Issue 1 — The single biggest leak is application_started → document_uploaded (86.8% loss)

13.24% step-through dwarfs every other stage's loss — bigger than the payment-step leak (47.86% step-through) and the initial browse-to-apply leak (15.44%) combined in relative terms. This is where the majority of "applications" simply disappear, and `base_context.md` does not mention it at all.

### Issue 2 — The H1 portfolio-wide conversion decline is real, and now localized to one specific step

Application→purchase conversion fell from 4.94% (Jan) to 3.96% (June), a ~20% relative drop, confirmed live by month:

| Month | Applications | Purchases | Conv % |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2026-01 | 21,580 | 1,066 | 4.94% |
| 2026-02 | 21,211 | 1,000 | 4.71% |
| 2026-03 | 25,298 | 1,167 | 4.61% |
| 2026-04 | 26,280 | 1,292 | 4.92% |
| 2026-05 | 29,665 | 1,331 | 4.49% |
| 2026-06 | 30,370 | 1,204 | 3.96% |

Decomposing by stage (all queried live) shows the decline is **not** coming from the payment step, which is flat all year (pay_now_clicked→purchase_completed: 49.8% Jan → 47.6% June, no trend), and only mildly from the top of the funnel (application_started→document_uploaded: 13.3% Jan → 12.4% June). It is concentrated in **document_uploaded → pay_now_clicked**, which erodes steadily from **74.5% (Jan) to 67.1% (June)** — a real ~7pp fall. That timing lines up with the known Android passport-capture regression (K2, re-verified live below), which also inflects in April and keeps worsening through June — a plausible, though not proven, contributing driver (K2's quality flag is measured on document_uploaded rows themselves, not a direct predictor of who proceeds to pay, so this is a correlational, not causal, link). Three alternative explanations for the broad decline were tested previously and refuted: Schengen summer scarcity (K4 — Schengen isn't distinctly worse), the 7.45 app rollout (K7 — `app_version` carries no real temporal signal), and the SUMMER20 campaign (K6 — it's an always-on code, not seasonal).

### Issue 3 — Android passport-capture failures are accelerating (K2), re-verified live and still the highest-priority finding

| Month | Android fail % | iOS fail % |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2026-01 | 6.64% | 8.21% |
| 2026-02 | 9.33% | 9.08% |
| 2026-03 | 7.88% | 8.28% |
| 2026-04 | 12.05% | 8.33% |
| 2026-05 | 23.07% | 8.09% |
| 2026-06 | **33.76%** | 10.16% |

Android's failure rate rose ~5x since April while iOS stayed flat — by June, roughly 1 in 3 Android document-capture attempts is flagged. `base_context.md` frames this as "some devices... being monitored"; the live data says it's a severe, still-worsening regression concentrated in exactly the step (document upload) driving Issue 2. Caveat: the underlying flag (`is_crossed_failed_attempt_threshold`) is internally inconsistent (D3 — 71.4% of flagged events had zero retries), so the absolute rate should be read with caution, but the trend (monotonic, Android-only, correctly timed) is robust.

### Issue 4 — pay_now_clicked → purchase_completed still loses 52% of payment intents, with no confirmed explanation

This step is large (14,739 → 7,054) and stable, not improving. The one candidate theory in `base_context.md` — an iOS/WebKit OTP regression hitting Gulf card users hardest (K1) — is refuted on this funnel: iOS is the best-converting high-volume platform (49.88% vs. Android 46.77%), and in the UAE specifically iOS beats Android by 27pp, the opposite of the claim. (A narrower, real iOS-only OTP-step regression was separately confirmed in the standalone Express Checkout flow, but that cannot be joined to this main funnel — see known_issues.md D2 — so it does not explain this leak.) This remains a large, real, and currently unattributed loss.

### Issue 5 — A silent, un-analyzed cohort exists before the funnel even starts

Live-confirmed: of 183,790 users who complete `auth_completed`, **29,377 (16.0%) never start an application at all.** `auth_completed` is a superset of the funnel's first analyzed stage, not a peer of it, and this cohort — people who log in but never even begin applying — sits entirely outside every dashboard built on `application_started` onward.

### Bottom line

Ranked by importance: (1) the 86.8% application→document-upload leak is the single largest drop in absolute terms; (2) the H1 conversion decline is real and now traced specifically to the document-upload→pay-click step, plausibly linked to (3) the accelerating Android capture-quality regression; (4) the 52% payment-intent leak remains large and unexplained by any tested theory; (5) 29,377 authenticated-but-never-applied users are an unaddressed pre-funnel cohort. Any funnel tooling must count by set membership, not `windowFunnel`, or conversion will read as 2.18% instead of the true 4.57%.
Where are we losing conversions, and for which segments (device / geo / destination) visualize it based on segments

Live query against `clickathon` (H1 2026 main funnel, `destination_card_clicked` → `application_started` → `document_uploaded` → `pay_now_clicked` → `purchase_completed`, computed by **set membership** per `known_issues.md` D1, not `windowFunnel`, which would understate late-funnel loss by 52%) confirms the two real leaks and shows they are **not evenly distributed across device, geo, or destination**.

**Where the loss happens (stage-level, all segments combined):**
- `application_started → document_uploaded`: **86.76% drop** (133,967 users lost) — the single largest absolute leak, and it is essentially **flat across every device type** (13.0%–13.6% step-through everywhere), so this leak is a product/UX problem, not a segment problem.
- `pay_now_clicked → purchase_completed`: **52.14% drop** (7,685 users lost) — the second-biggest leak, and this is where almost all the segment variation concentrates.

**By device** (`funnel_conversion` = purchased ÷ started; n = 154,413 started):
| Device | Started | Purchased | Funnel conversion | pay→purchase rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| iOS | 63,520 | 3,193 | **5.03%** (best) | 49.88% |
| Desktop | 10,655 | 499 | 4.68% | 46.51% |
| web-user-b2c | 30,611 | 1,335 | 4.36% | 46.08% |
| Android | 49,627 | 2,027 | **4.08%** (worst) | 46.41% |

~1pp spread, driven almost entirely at the payment step (iOS 49.9% vs. Android 46.4%), not the doc-upload step. Note: `known_issues.md` K1 ("Gulf/iOS pay-step abandonment") is refuted — iOS is consistently the *best*-converting platform here, consistent with K1's prior refutation on this same funnel.

**By geo** (`geoip_country_code`, top 10 by volume):
| Geo | Started | Purchased | Funnel conversion | pay→purchase rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AE | 21,630 | 1,163 | **5.38%** (best) | 56.24% |
| QA | 3,163 | 152 | 4.81% | 46.77% |
| GB | 6,183 | 293 | 4.74% | 49.16% |
| OM | 2,581 | 119 | 4.61% | 51.74% |
| OTHER | 13,600 | 623 | 4.58% | 45.08% |
| AU | 5,949 | 277 | 4.66% | 46.79% |
| SA | 4,716 | 212 | 4.50% | 48.74% |
| IN | 86,506 | 3,791 | 4.38% | 46.18% |
| US | 7,756 | 338 | 4.36% | 48.70% |
| SG | 2,329 | 86 | **3.69%** (worst) | 41.35% |

~1.7pp spread (AE 5.38% vs. SG 3.69%), again mostly explained by the pay→purchase step (AE 56.2% vs. SG 41.4%). India, the dominant volume geo (86,506 started, 56% of all applications), sits mid-pack at 4.38%.

**By destination** (27 values, `application_started → purchase_completed`):
Best: QA (**5.69%**, n=1,651), FR (5.29%), OM (5.19%). Worst: KR (**4.11%**, n=1,192), ID (4.23%), TH (4.31%). Spread is ~1.6pp — modest and with no obvious regional clustering (Gulf destinations span both the best, QA, and only-mid, AE at 4.40%).

**Bottom line:** the biggest, actionable leak (application → document upload, 86.76%) is uniform across segments — fixing it is a product change, not a targeting one. The smaller pay→purchase leak (52.14%) is where device/geo/destination actually matter, with a consistent ~1.5–2pp spread everywhere, and no known issue in the wiki (K1, K4 checked and refuted) explains it — it lines up with the unexplained 20% relative decline in overall `funnel_conversion` across H1 2026 (4.91%→3.93%) noted in `metrics/funnel_conversion.md`.

Scope: H1 2026 baseline data (2025-12-31→2026-07-01), 1,000,000 card-clicks → 7,054 purchases, all counts by exact `uniqExact(user_id)` set membership (funnel is perfectly nested, so no join was required for the un-segmented counts). See the full report: q02_report.html.

Where are we losing conversions?

Main visa-application funnel, segmented by device / geo / destination — live query against clickathon
Scope: H1 2026 baseline data (2025‑12‑31 23:41 → 2026‑07‑01 03:01), 1,000,000 destination_card_clicked users → 7,054 purchase_completed users. All counts computed by exact uniqExact(user_id) set membership — not windowFunnel, which understates late‑funnel conversion by ~52% on this dataset (known data trap D1). Query run 2026‑08‑02.

1. The funnel — two real leaks

Bar width is log‑scaled (raw counts span 1,000,000 → 7,054); the label on each bar is the true user count. The number between bars is the drop‑off at that step.
86.76%
application started → document uploaded — 133,967 users lost, the largest absolute leak, and (see §2) flat across every device segment. A product/UX problem, not a targeting problem.
52.14%
pay now clicked → purchase completed — 7,685 users lost. Smaller in absolute terms but this is where nearly all the device/geo/destination variation shown below concentrates.

2. By device

Funnel conversion = purchased ÷ started (n = 154,413 started). The paired bar shows the pay‑now → purchase rate — the step where the device gap actually opens up; the earlier application → document‑upload step is flat (13.0%–13.6%) across all four devices.
Funnel conversion (purchased ÷ started) Pay‑now → purchase rate

3. By geo (geoip_country_code)

Funnel conversion by country, sorted descending, top 10 by volume. India is the dominant volume geo (86,506 started, 56% of all applications) but sits mid‑pack on conversion.

4. By destination

Funnel conversion by destination country, all 27 values, sorted descending. Spread is the narrowest of the three cuts (~1.6pp, KR to QA) with no obvious regional clustering — Gulf destinations span both the best (QA) and only mid‑pack (AE).

Takeaways

  • Fix the big one first: 86.76% of started applications never upload a document — uniform across every segment cut here, so it's a UX/flow fix, not a segment‑targeted one.
  • The segment-sensitive leak is at payment: pay‑now → purchase swings ~9pp by geo (AE 56.2% vs SG 41.4%) and ~4pp by device (iOS 49.9% vs Android 46.4%). No known issue in the wiki explains it — K1 ("Gulf/iOS abandon at pay step") is refuted here too: iOS is the best-converting device, and AE the best-converting geo, both against K1's prediction.
  • Overall funnel conversion is declining ~20% relative across H1 (4.91% → 3.93%, per metrics/funnel_conversion.md), unexplained by K4 (refuted as Schengen‑specific). This decline is broader than any single segment shown here and worth flagging as an open question.

messages.content: Visualize regressions or trends over the last quarter?

Scope: "last quarter" = Q2 2026 (2026-04-01 → 2026-06-30), the last full calendar quarter as of today (2026-08-02) and fully within the live data window. Queried live against `application_started`, `purchase_completed`, `document_uploaded`, `pay_now_clicked`, `destination_card_clicked` in `clickathon` (2026-08-02). Funnel conversion was computed by set-membership join on `user_id`, per known_issues.md D1 (not `windowFunnel`, which loses ~52% of conversions on this data).

**Headline regression — Android document-capture failures, up ~5x (K2, reconfirmed):** weekly `is_crossed_failed_attempt_threshold` rate on `document_uploaded` rose almost every week of Q2 — 7.4% (Apr 5) → 10.6% → 9.1% → 19.6% → 21.5% → 23.8% → 22.8% → 27.4% → 30.9% → 32.4% → 30.0% → 34.3% (Jun 21), monthly 11.69%→23.43%→33.54%. iOS stayed flat all quarter (7.5%–10.8%, monthly 8.33%/8.09%/10.16%). This is an exact live reproduction of known_issues.md → K2, still accelerating in the most recent week measured. Caveat (D3): this flag doesn't reliably track true capture quality elsewhere in the data (71.4% of flagged events have zero retries), so the *trend* is robust but the *absolute level* carries some doubt.

**Trend — funnel conversion kept sliding:** application→purchase conversion fell from ~4.9–5.1% in early April to ~3.7–4.0% by June (monthly: 4.92% Apr → 4.49% May → 3.96% Jun), continuing the broad H1 2026 decline already on record (business.md: 4.91%→3.93%, Jan→Jun) — present in essentially every week of Q2, not a one-month blip. This dataset can't attribute a cause to it (K4 Schengen-seasonality and K6 SUMMER20-campaign explanations are both refuted elsewhere in known_issues.md).

**Not a regression — funnel volume:** indexing each stage to its Apr-5 week (=100), top-of-funnel traffic (card clicks, applications) grew a steady ~18–20% across the quarter — healthy organic growth. But `pay_now_clicked` and `purchase_completed` volumes stayed roughly flat, dipping below their April baseline in several weeks — the flip side of the declining conversion rate: more people entering the funnel, a shrinking share coming out the other end.

Sample/scope: 12 full ISO weeks (Apr 5 – Jun 27 2026; the partial first/last calendar weeks of the query window were excluded from the weekly charts), ~85,000 applications and ~3,500 purchases in Q2. See the full report with charts: q03_report.html.
